entries.rationale: U+FEFF leading a text node, as a UTF-8-with-BOM resource file produces. Invisible on screen and in most diffs, but the string is unequal to its own literal on the first character.

The shell is served as UTF-8-with-BOM. The BOM sits before the doctype, so a parser may treat it as content and some clients render a stray glyph. This is the flavour a detector reading the declared charset should catch.
Company name, deliberately in Latin script on the Hindi page.
Product name in Latin script. A script-violation check that flags Latin characters on a Devanagari page will fire here, and be wrong.
Latin digits are the overwhelming convention in Hindi web content. Demanding Devanagari numerals (२४०) would be wrong for this market.
A release number. Applying Indian digit grouping to it would produce nonsense.
A product code, not a date.
The registered Indian entity name. Written in Latin script by law, on the Hindi page.
